\[
x=\rho \sin\phi \cos\theta,\quad y=\rho \sin\phi \sin\theta,\quad z=\rho \cos\phi,
\]
the diametrically opposite point has coordinates \((-x,-y,-z)\).

Thus:
- \(\rho\) stays the same: \(\rho=3\).
- The polar angle becomes \(\phi'=\pi-\phi=\pi-\frac{\pi}{5}=\frac{4\pi}{5}\).
- The azimuthal angle becomes \(\theta'=\theta+\pi=\frac{3\pi}{8}+\pi=\frac{11\pi}{8}\).

So the spherical coordinates are
\[
\left(3,\frac{11\pi}{8},\frac{4\pi}{5}\right).
\]
